diagnostics.message: aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up must wait for aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up to grant the execution role SQS receive/delete/get-attributes permissions; referencing the function and queue alone does not order policy creation, so mapping creation can fail authorization.

aws_lambda_function.webhook must wait for webhook_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured: Lambda creation requires the execution role's ENI permissions, which the role ARN reference does not include.
aws_lambda_function.scale_up must wait for scale_up_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured, so its execution role has ENI permissions before VPC-enabled function creation.
aws_lambda_function.scale_down must wait for scale_down_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured, so its execution role has ENI permissions before VPC-enabled function creation.
aws_lambda_function.pool must wait for pool_vpc_execution_role when the pool and VPC subnets are configured, so its execution role has ENI permissions before VPC-enabled function creation.
aws_lambda_function.syncer must wait for syncer_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured, so its execution role has ENI permissions before VPC-enabled function creation.

aws_s3_object.trigger immediately invokes the syncer through S3 notifications but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy.syncer. Wait for its S3 permissions before uploading the initial trigger to avoid an initial sync failing with AccessDenied.

aws_s3_object.trigger should wait for aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_kms when a KMS key is configured: uploading this object immediately invokes the syncer, which needs its KMS permissions to write the encrypted distribution.

aws_s3_object.trigger should wait for aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging. Its upload immediately invokes the syncer, while neither the notification nor the function reference waits for logging permissions; the initial invocation can otherwise lose its logs.
